results.title: Difference Studies with Staggered Treatment Adoption
results.content: Constraints like this might be desirable in applications in which researchers wish to estimate a sequence of post-adoption ATT s for each timing group and want to ensure that variation in treatment effects from one period to the next does not arise because of changes in the composition of the control group. In addition to estimating a sequence of time-varying treatment effects for each adoption group, the staggered adoption design also allows researchers to construct partial tests of the common trends and no anticipation assumptions using the same approach described for event study designs. Gardner (14) takes a different approach by setting up a two-step regression-based method that estimates the group- and time-fixed effects using only untreated observations before estimating the treatment effects.Finally,de Chaisemartin & D’Haultfoeuille (9) build an estimator focused on comparing changes in treated units just before and after treatment to units that do not experience a change at that time.
